candidates.statement: Therefore, one should always verify whether a classical $t$-deformed curve actually admits a consistent quantization.
We should stress that this issue of quantizability is much more delicate for refined $A$-polynomials compared to the ordinary ones.
Hence, at first it may not be entirely obvious how to reconcile arbitrariness of $t$ with the fact that certain functions of this parameter should satisfy rather strong constraints.
However, the condition ([\[qcond0\]](#qcond0){reference-type="ref" reference="qcond0"}) means that $\eta(x,y)$ must actually be exact.
In the language of algebraic K-theory, this means that the symbol $\{ x,y \} = 0$ must be trivial in $K_2 ({\mathbb C}({\cal C })) \otimes {\mathbb Q}$.

The condition ([\[tempered\]](#tempered){reference-type="ref" reference="tempered"}) states that all roots of face polynomials $f(z)$, constructed for all boundaries of the Newton polygon, must be roots of unity.
It is this latter condition that we shall consider below in order to test quantizability of the refined $A$-polynomials.
If we insist that the criterion ([\[tempered\]](#tempered){reference-type="ref" reference="tempered"}) should be satisfied, we conclude that the deformation parameter $t$ should be a root of unity.

Interestingly, all these polynomials factor into linear factors in $z$, and the constraint ([\[tempered\]](#tempered){reference-type="ref" reference="tempered"}) again leads to the aforementioned conclusion: the deformation parameter $t$ must be a root of unity.
Conjecturally, these amplitudes should be reproduced by a refined version of topological string theory on a toric Calabi-Yau manifold.

candidates.statement: In arbitrary framing such an amplitude reads $$Z_{\text{BPS}}^{\text{open}} \; = \; \sum_R f_R(q_1,q_2)^{-f} C_{\bullet\bullet R}(q_1^{-1},q_2^{-1}) s_R(x) \,.$$ Performing the summation we get $$Z_{\text{BPS}}^{\text{open}} \; = \; \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} (-1)^{(f+1)k} q_2^{\frac{f}{2}k(k-1)} \Big(x \frac{q_1}{\sqrt{q_2}}\Big)^k \prod_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{1 - q_1 q_2^{i-1}} \,. \label{Zopen-BPS-C3}$$ For $f=0$ this result reduces, as it should, to the brane amplitude in ${\mathbb C}^3$ in phase III found in [@Iqbal:2007ii] (after identifying $x=-Q$).
Therefore, the quantizability conditions should impose some constraints on $q_1$ as well as on $Q_i$, and this is indeed what happens.
In the conifold case, we find that both $q_1$ and $Q$ must be roots of unity.
This imposes an interesting condition on the Kähler parameter: $\log Q$ must be a pure imaginary rational number.

In particular, the Yang-Yang function of the quantum integrable system is identified with the following limit of the instanton partition function in the absence of any surface operators [@NS]: $$\lim_{\epsilon_1 \to 0} \, \epsilon_1 \, \log Z_{\text{BPS}}^{\text{closed}} (\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2) \; = \; \frac{1}{\epsilon_2} {\mathcal{F}}^{(0)} + {\mathcal{F}}^{(1)} + {\cal O }(\epsilon_2) \label{YangYang}$$ This expansion should not be confused with a similar-looking expansion in [\[ZopenW\]](#ZopenW){reference-type="eqref" reference="ZopenW"}, which describes the behavior of the *open* BPS partition function or, from the gauge theory viewpoint, represents the contribution of a surface operator.
